title: AI-assisted preoperative planning improves component sizing accuracy in Oxford unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: a retrospective cohort study with 24-month follow-up.
summary: Specific clinical planning accuracy result measured against operative sizing; retrospective cohort qualifies narrowly. Do not imply improved patient outcomes; modest HSS difference and single-center/nonrandomized design are material limits.
ai_technology: 190 knees (AI-assisted n=94, conventional n=96), 3D patient-specific CT bone model and deep-learning landmarks used in preoperative sizing plan; postoperative component size compared with intraoperative sizing. Femoral accuracy 77/94 (81.91%), tibial 80/94 (85.12%), both 66/94 (70.21%). HSS difference 3.18 at 24 months is modest and retrospective nonrandomized design does not establish clinical benefit.
